newsitem.title: USA: Sun Microsystems stock falls after price cuts.
newsitem.headline: Sun Microsystems stock falls after price cuts.

text.p: Sun Microsystems Inc. stock tumbled in heavy trading Wednesday, a day after the computer maker cut prices on some of its most popular models.
The stock fell $3.625 to $57.75 on Nasdaq, where it was one of the most active issues with more than 12.9 million shares traded.

On Tuesday, Sun slashed prices by up to 38 percent on its popular line of UltraComputing desktop computers and its workgroup servers, the type of machines that control the flow of information through networks.
Mountain View, Calif.-based Sun said the price cuts were part of a plan to increase its share of the workstation and server markets.
In recent months, Sun, a maker of high-end computers, has faced increasing competition from companies such as Compaq Computer Corp. and Dell Computer Corp.
Compaq, Dell and other personal computer makers are offering machines comparable to Sun in computing power, but at much lower prices.
